newsitem.title: USA: Ferraro would beat D'Amato for U.S. Senate -- poll.
newsitem.headline: Ferraro would beat D'Amato for U.S. Senate -- poll.

text.p: Former Democrat vice presidential candidate Geraldine Ferraro would beat Sen. Alfonse D'Amato, R-N.Y., if the two were to run against each other in 1998, a new poll showed.

Ferraro, who served as a Representative for New York State before she was picked for the second spot on the Democrat ticket in 1984, would do better than other Democrats considering whether to challenge D'Amato.

But the poll, conducted Feb 24 to March 2 by Quinnipiac College, also showed that the Republican incumbent's approval ratings, though still negative by a 40 percent to 50 percent margin, have improved from the 33 percent to 58 percent reading seen on June 20, 1996.

D'Amato, a key figure in state politics who is seen as Gov. George Pataki's mentor, scored best on his ability to get things done, as 72 percent to 21 percent of the 1,071 New Yorkers who said they were registered voters agreed on this subject.
"New Yorkers respect Sen. D'Amato for getting things done, but they don't admire him," said Maurice Carroll, the polling institute's director, in prepared remarks.

Yet New York City Public Advocate Mark Green would win a race against D'Amato by a 47 percent to 35 percent margin, while Brooklyn Congressman Charles Schumer would beat him by 43 percent to 36 percent, the survey found.

The junior Republican Senator, however, also scored well for having strong leadership qualities, a statement agreed with by 63 percent to 31 percent of those surveyed. And 52 percent to 35 percent said he worked well with other political leaders.
On the negative side, only a minority -- 36 percent to 55 percent -- thought he had a likable personality, and only 30 percent to 58 percent said he was honest and trustworthy.
